clue.text: Short religious book found in diocese, written round about 250

indicators.note: one set of letters is found inside the other, so they go into the middle
the word for a diocese is written round the other way, i.e. back to front

parts.note: a bishop's see is his diocese
C is short for circa, Latin for about
CL is 250 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A pocket-sized scripture turns up somewhere in a diocese, dated to about AD 250.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written round' reverses the diocese word to EES. Eccles is also a town in Greater Manchester, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles. is the standard abbreviated title of the Old Testament book Ecclesiastes.

clue.text: The writer served up crackers and cheese

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters are read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to himself as me
crackers and mental both mean mad, informally

explanation.surface: The writer offers crackers and cheese, like a host serving a cheeseboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the biscuits for the cheese but means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmental is a Swiss cheese with holes, a variety of cheese.

clue.text: North American woman with Russian name apparently imprisoned?

indicators.note: flags reading imprisoned literally as 'in can', so the name is placed within the word can

parts.note: the can is slang for prison, so someone imprisoned is in the can
Nadia is a woman's name of Russian origin

explanation.surface: A North American woman whose name sounds Russian seems to have been locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoned' does double work: it supplies the container and, as 'in can', says where the name goes, with 'apparently' flagging the literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A Canadian is a native of Canada, a country in North America.

clue.text: Gent's undies regularly removed for exercise

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is removed, keeping the rest

explanation.surface: A man's underwear is taken off at intervals for a workout.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the 1st, 3rd, 5th letters and so on of GENTSUNDIES, keeping E, T, U, D, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An étude is a musical study, a piece written as practice for a performer's technique.

clue.text: Well-heeled demi-mondaine provides American capital

parts.note: well-heeled means wealthy, rich

indicators.note: demi means half, so only the first half of the word mondaine is taken

explanation.surface: A wealthy courtesan bankrolls a capital city in America.
explanation.walkthrough: A demi-mondaine is a kept woman, but the prefix here halves MONDAINE to MOND.
explanation.definitionFit: Richmond is the state capital of Virginia and was the Confederate capital.

clue.text: Greeks charge carriers for carrying one article

indicators.note: the first word holds the others inside it, as a carrier would

parts.note: ions are atoms or molecules that carry an electric charge
I is the Roman numeral one
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Greek porters bill for carrying a single item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge carriers' reads like fee collectors but means electrically charged particles.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ionians were one of the ancient Greek peoples, settled in Ionia.

clue.text: US author for one visits bogus healer

indicators.note: one piece calls in on the other, ending up inside it
bogus means fake, so the letters of healer are not in their true order

parts.note: per means for each, i.e. for one

explanation.surface: An American writer, say, calls on a quack healer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bogus' scrambles the healer into HARLEE before 'visits' takes effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Harper Lee was the American novelist who wrote To Kill a Mockingbird.

clue.text: Athletic team's possible cause of food poisoning?

definitions.meaning: ... Athletic is an English football club from Greater Manchester
..., meat past its best, might make you ill

explanation.surface: A sports club is blamed for a bout of food poisoning.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is'. Oldham is a town in Greater Manchester whose football club is Oldham Athletic.
explanation.definitionFit: The football club is commonly called simply Oldham, and stale ham is a plausible food hazard.

clue.text: Actor from Brazil employed in Droylsden ironworks

indicators.note: the answer works inside these words, its letters running across them

explanation.surface: A Brazilian actor has taken a job in a Manchester-area ironworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brazil' is not the country but Terry Gilliam's 1985 film, in which Robert De Niro played a role. Droylsden is a town near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert De Niro appeared in the film Brazil as the renegade heating engineer Tuttle.

clue.text: Hard cheese, having lost way in Paris?

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

indicators.note: the cheese loses the letters for a way, which are taken out

parts.note: Stilton is an English blue cheese
St is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A tough cheese gets lost on the way somewhere in Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris?' is not the city but the celebrity Paris Hilton; the question mark flags the first name standing for the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris Hilton is the hotel heiress, so her surname is the one Paris points to.

clue.text: A manic nun mithered a northerner

indicators.note: mithered is northern dialect for bothered or fussed, so the letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A frantic nun pesters someone from the north of England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mithered' is a word used in Manchester itself, which suits the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mancunian is a native of Manchester, a city in the north of England.

clue.text: Cook overcome by diffused gas

indicators.note: one word is covered over by the other, so it sits inside it

parts.note: dye that ran has spread or diffused
to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: A cook is overwhelmed by gas spreading through the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'diffused' looks like it describes the gas but it gives RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Radon is a radioactive noble gas, element 86.

clue.text: Bit of glass lodged in bare butt

indicators.note: the small piece is stuck inside the longer word

parts.note: bare means naked, nude

indicators.note: only a small part, the first letter, of the word glass is used

explanation.surface: A shard of glass gets stuck in someone's bare backside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butt' looks like a noun, the bottom, but is the verb to push.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt and to nudge both mean to push at something, here as verbs.

clue.text: Exhibition featuring jazz, close to Sloane Square

parts.note: trad is traditional jazz

indicators.note: the close of the word, its last letter, is taken

parts.note: square means fair or honest

explanation.surface: A show with live jazz near Sloane Square, the smart London square.
explanation.walkthrough: Sloane Square is a fashionable square in Chelsea, London; here 'Square' gives FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade fair is an exhibition where businesses display their products.

clue.text: Uninhibitedness in a strip club? Not half

parts.note: a band is a strip of material

indicators.note: not the first half of the word for a club, so only its second half is kept

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Freedom from restraint in a strip club? Very much so, as in 'not half!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' reads as the British exclamation meaning 'definitely', but removes IR from IRON, leaving ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Abandon as a noun means a complete lack of restraint or inhibition.

clue.text: Kurds darn pants — tight ones

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are badly arranged

explanation.surface: Kurdish people mend trousers that are too tight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' looks like trousers being darned but means rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tight is slang for drunk, so tight ones are drunkards.

clue.text: Fantastic deals? Daughter's going here

indicators.note: fantastic means fanciful, so the remaining letters are rearranged freely
the daughter's going means that letter leaves the word deals

explanation.surface: A shop offers amazing bargains, so a daughter heads there.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove D from DEALS and rearrange EALS. Sale is also a town in Greater Manchester, the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A sale is an event of discounted prices, where great bargains are found.

clue.text: Refreshment for most of army with tea to drink

indicators.note: re-freshing these letters means making them anew in a fresh order
most of the word army is used, its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: The troops are refreshed with tea to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refreshment' reads as tea for soldiers but means 're-fresh': ARM and TEA are rearranged, and 'to' follows as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur, a drink.

clue.text: Some have delusions of this German currency dominating another mostly

indicators.note: in a down clue, dominating means sitting on top, placed before the rest

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

indicators.note: most of the word for another currency is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: another currency here, the euro

explanation.surface: German money overpowering a rival currency gives some people delusions of grandeur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another currency: EURO, which 'mostly' cuts to EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'delusions of grandeur' means an inflated sense of one's own importance.

clue.text: Deal with dead fruit when delivered

indicators.note: a speech is delivered when spoken, so the word is taken as heard

parts.note: a berry is a small fruit

explanation.surface: Handling dead fruit when it arrives from the supplier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delivered' suggests a grocer's order but means spoken. Bury is also a town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury the dead is to put them in the ground, how dead bodies are dealt with.

clue.text: Open University dons also in the old capital

indicators.note: the built-up letters go in the old word for the

parts.note: ye is an old form of the

indicators.note: also dons, i.e. puts on, the university, so it is wrapped round it

parts.note: and means also

explanation.surface: Open University lecturers are also found in the former capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dons' reads as academics but is the verb 'puts on', making AOUND; Yaoundé is the current capital of Cameroon, so 'the old' is not the time-word it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Yaoundé is the capital city of Cameroon.

clue.text: Papers penned by revolutionary left-wing idealist

indicators.note: the papers are enclosed, as in a pen, by the other letters
revolutionary means turning round, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: red is a left-wing person
a ream is a quantity of paper

explanation.surface: Articles written by a radical socialist dreamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reads as describing a political rebel but signals turning RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone with unrealistic ideals, an idealist.

clue.text: American lawyer set to defend one English case

parts.note: DA is a District Attorney in the US

indicators.note: the set protects one by surrounding it

parts.note: a TV set
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A US attorney is ready to defend an English client's case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is grammatical, not legal; 'set' is a television set.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, used for indirect objects in languages like German.

clue.text: A dandy to boot

parts.note: a swell is a fashionably dressed man, a dandy

explanation.surface: A fop thrown in as an extra, a bonus companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to boot' sounds like footwear for a dandy but means in addition.
explanation.definitionFit: To boot is an idiom meaning in addition, also.

clue.text: Michael who sings Keep On Running

definitions.meaning: to bolt is to run, so ... would mean keep on running

explanation.surface: Michael who sings the song Keep On Running.
explanation.walkthrough: Keep On Running is a 1960s hit by the Spencer Davis Group. Bolton is a town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Bolton is the singer of power ballads; bolting on means continuing to run.

clue.text: A place to keep wine

parts.note: a shop that keeps an item is said to stock it
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Looking for somewhere to store wine, like a cellar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A place' looks like the start of a definition of a cellar but is the definition itself: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Stockport is a town in Greater Manchester, a place on the map.

clue.text: Horse shakes off one bird

indicators.note: the drug gets rid of the letter for one

parts.note: horse is slang for heroin
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A horse throws its rider, a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is drug slang for heroin; the image of shaking off a habit fits.
explanation.definitionFit: A heron is a long-legged wading bird.

clue.text: Line penned by Scottish philosopher and poet

indicators.note: the line is enclosed in the philosopher's name, as in a pen

parts.note: David Hume was an 18th-century Scottish philosopher

explanation.surface: A line written by a Scottish philosopher who also wrote poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and poet' looks like a second description of the philosopher, but 'poet' is the definition, joined by 'and'. Hulme is also a district of Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: T. E. Hulme was an English poet and critic, an early Imagist.

clue.text: Fruit supply in a tree

indicators.note: read as supple-y, bending flexibly, so these letters bend into a new order

explanation.surface: A tree yields a supply of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the noun but the adverb from supple, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An eater is a dessert apple or other fruit for eating raw rather than cooking.

clue.text: Short book Harry lent to Eve

indicators.note: to harry is to harass, so these letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A slim volume that a man called Harry lent to Eve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like a name but is the verb, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel, a brief work of fiction.

clue.text: English painter left with Sibyl?

parts.note: and means with, along with
a sibyl was a prophetess, a seer

explanation.surface: An English artist is left in the company of a woman called Sibyl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sibyl' looks like a woman's name but is a prophetess.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian English painter, famous for animals and the Trafalgar Square lions.

clue.text: Alternative route from Hyde to Urmston

indicators.note: the answer is taken from within these words, across them

explanation.surface: A different way to travel between two Manchester-area towns, Hyde and Urmston.
explanation.walkthrough: Hyde and Urmston are towns in Greater Manchester, matching the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a roundabout way taken instead of the usual direct one.
